title: The Basement Delivery
premise: A courier starts two floors below ground and must rise five floors, but treats the ground-floor label as an extra step. A numbered elevator track exposes the counting error and delivers the parcel to floor three.
hook: Five floors up from minus two: where do we land?
visible_action: An elevator advances one tick per beat; a ghost counter incorrectly counts the starting floor.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Movement on a number line counts intervals, not the starting position.
gate: Keep floor numbering explicitly mathematical rather than a real building convention.

style_application.material: Crisp lines and restrained chalk labels
style_application.why: Intervals can be counted without visual depth confusing the starting point.
style_application.check: Check signed arithmetic and keep the same unit spacing.

editorial_pick.original_reason: The mistaken count is small, concrete and can be demonstrated without a complex asset set.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: An elevator travels on a clearly mathematical number line while a second counter exposes the off-by-one error.
editorial_pick.gate: Verify the signed arithmetic. Explain that floor labels are a model rather than a real building standard.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
